chokepoints.name: Strait of Hormuz
chokepoints.status_note: Closed to most commercial traffic since 2 Mar 2026 after US–Israeli strikes on Iran. IMF PortWatch logged 0–8 transits a day in September 2026 against roughly 100 a day in 2025. The US has blockaded Iranian ports since April; a June truce collapsed in July.
chokepoints.share_note: ≈20% of world petroleum-liquids consumption and >20% of global LNG trade (1H25).

bypass.name: Saudi East–West pipeline (Abqaiq → Yanbu)
bypass.note: Record 7 mb/d in 1Q26; shut by drone strikes 13 Sep 2026, restarted 22 Sep.

bypass.name: Iraq Kirkuk → Ceyhan (Türkiye)
bypass.note: Restarted 27 Sep 2025 after a 2½-year halt; nameplate far higher.

sources.label: EIA, World Oil Transit Chokepoints (updated 3 Mar 2026)
CNN, 13 Sep 2026: Iran–Gulf talks on reopening Hormuz postponed

chokepoints.name: Strait of Malacca
chokepoints.status_note: Open. Volumes are depressed because Gulf crude bound for East Asia is stranded behind Hormuz.
chokepoints.share_note: Largest oil chokepoint: ≈29% of seaborne oil (1H25). China takes ~48% of volumes.

sources.label: EIA, World Oil Transit Chokepoints (updated 3 Mar 2026)

chokepoints.name: Suez Canal & SUMED
chokepoints.status_note: Open, but volumes remain about half of 2023 levels because of the Red Sea security crisis.
chokepoints.share_note: SUMED pipeline capacity 2.5 mb/d (Ain Sukhna → Sidi Kerir).

sources.label: EIA, World Oil Transit Chokepoints (updated 3 Mar 2026)

chokepoints.name: Bab el-Mandeb
chokepoints.status_note: By September 2026 the Houthis held Yemen's whole Red Sea coast, including Perim island at the strait. They have attacked Saudi-linked shipping. LNG carriers have avoided the route entirely since 2024.
chokepoints.share_note: Down ~55% from 2023; flows rerouted around the Cape of Good Hope.

sources.label: EIA, World Oil Transit Chokepoints (updated 3 Mar 2026)
Al Jazeera, 13 Sep 2026: Houthis seize Bab al-Mandeb strait

chokepoints.name: Cape of Good Hope
chokepoints.status_note: Not a chokepoint, but it has become the main detour for Atlantic–Asia trade since late 2023.

sources.label: EIA, World Oil Transit Chokepoints (updated 3 Mar 2026)

chokepoints.name: Turkish Straits
chokepoints.status_note: Open. Kazakh CPC crude is the largest flow. LNG is barred from the Bosporus.
chokepoints.share_note: Bosporus figures; the Dardanelles carried 3.7 mb/d in 1H25.

sources.label: EIA, World Oil Transit Chokepoints (updated 3 Mar 2026)

chokepoints.name: Danish Straits
chokepoints.status_note: Open. This is the main outlet for Russian Baltic crude and products.
chokepoints.share_note: ≈6% of seaborne oil. PortWatch series shown is the Øresund.

sources.label: EIA, World Oil Transit Chokepoints (updated 3 Mar 2026)

chokepoints.name: Panama Canal
chokepoints.status_note: Open, and water levels have recovered from the 2023–24 drought. Mostly carries US refined products and LPG; LNG has largely moved to the Cape route.
